description: What the store worker does when a document's mounted browser actor is lost without anyone asking for it — an action invocation whose outcome it cannot confirm, a child fault while it applies an inbound hub frame, or a failed render turn. The actor is closed, the document's in-flight batches go back to the front of its outbox in batch order (confirmed local edits are never dropped and never sent twice: the outbox is id-deduplicated and the hub settles what it already holds), the document socket ends with the browser close row `actorLost`, and the reconnect loop reopens AT ONCE along the ordinary open path: a new open plan, a new lease, a fresh actor seeded from the hub's canonical checkpoint pair plus the tail since (the last confirmed frontier). The unconfirmed input is refused `not-applied` (retryable, never replayed by the shell). A loss counts toward the bound unless the actor had been mounted for stableAfterMs or an action was applied since the previous loss; more than maxConsecutiveLosses consecutive losses end the recovery with the typed fault `document-actor.recovery-exhausted` instead of a reconnect storm.

cases.name: one unconfirmed invocation reopens at once, and the next applied action clears the count
